items.stem: What distinguishes a 'blocking' review comment from a 'nit'?

options.text: A blocking comment identifies an issue that must be resolved before merge; a nit is a minor, optional suggestion
options.rationale: Correct: labelling severity helps authors prioritise.

options.text: A nit must always be fixed before merge
Blocking comments are only about formatting
options.rationale: Formatting is usually a nit, not blocking.
The distinction guides what gates the merge.

items.stem: Why are smaller pull requests generally easier to review well?

options.text: Reviewers can reason about the full change and catch more issues than in a large diff
options.rationale: Correct: review quality drops as diff size grows.

options.text: They always contain fewer bugs regardless of content

options.rationale: Size does not change CI behaviour.

items.stem: Which practices make code-review feedback more effective? (Select TWO)

options.text: Make comments specific and actionable, pointing to the line and a concrete suggestion
options.rationale: Correct: authors can act on precise feedback.

options.text: Critique the code, not the author
options.rationale: Correct: keeping it impersonal sustains a healthy culture.

options.text: Delay reviews indefinitely to be thorough
options.rationale: False; slow reviews block the team.

options.text: Block merges over personal style preferences
options.rationale: False; subjective nits should not gate merges.
